ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Talk It Out, Help Is Here

fullPassage:
Talk It Out, Help Is Here

Host: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. We have two special guests. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you to come up with the program?

Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring psychiatry into the community.

Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could you explain to us how the Friendship Bench program works?

Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.

Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program?

Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.

Host: That's interesting! What happens after patients complete their sessions with the grandmothers?

Dr. Chibanda: When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced similar struggles.

Host: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. And the program has been incredibly successful, right?

Dr. Chibanda: That's correct. In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. Our vision is for everyone to have a Friendship Bench within walking distance, and we are working hard to make it happen. We've also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app. This has helped us reach even more people.

Host: That's really amazing! Thank you for your time, Dr. Chibanda. Now let's hear from one of the grandmothers who volunteer for the program. Can you introduce yourself and tell us how you got involved with the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. I knew that I could help heal their wounded hearts by supporting them.

Host: That's very kind of you. Can you tell us about your experience as a grandmother for the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo: It's been wonderful. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I've seen how it can make a difference in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.

Host: Thanks for sharing your experiences with us today, Grandma Moyo. It's truly inspiring to see the influence that the Friendship Bench program has had. And it's all thanks to the hard work of people like you and Dr. Chibanda.

questions.passage: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe ①<u>called</u> Friendship Benches. First, please welcome the founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us ②<u>that</u> inspired you to come up with the program? The idea came from an experience I ③<u>had</u> as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely ④<u>depressed</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 무엇이 당신에게 영감을 주었는지 말씀해 주시겠어요?
det.analysis: ✅ ①called: 과거분사로 benches를 수식. '~라고 불리는'으로 정상. ❌ ②that: 원문은 what. 'tell us what inspired you'에서 what은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 inspired의 주어 역할. that은 선행사 없이 주어가 될 수 없음. ✅ ③had: 'an experience I had'에서 과거시제로 정상. ✅ ④depressed: 'had become depressed'에서 과거분사/형용사로 정상.
det.tip: what vs that: what = the thing that(~하는 것). 선행사를 포함하므로 앞에 명사가 없음. that은 선행사가 필요.

questions.passage: However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to ①<u>afford</u> the bus ride to the hospital. This ②<u>shocking</u> me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe ③<u>to pay</u> for transportation and ④<u>receive</u> medical treatment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이것은 저에게 충격을 주었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①afford: 'unable to afford'에서 to부정사 뒤 동사원형으로 정상. ❌ ②shocking: 원문은 shocked. 주어 This가 과거에 '충격을 주었다'는 완전한 문장의 동사가 필요. shocking(현재분사)은 동사 역할 불가. ✅ ③to pay: 가주어 it, 진주어 to pay 구문으로 정상. ✅ ④receive: to pay와 병렬로 연결된 동사원형으로 정상.
det.tip: shocked(과거형 동사) vs shocking(현재분사/형용사): 문장에서 동사가 필요한 자리에는 과거형 shocked가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to ①<u>sit</u> with patients at the benches, ②<u>listen</u> to their stories, and provide them with emotional support. Grandmothers ③<u>were chosen</u> for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. They have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent ④<u>listened</u> skills.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 뛰어난 경청 기술.
det.analysis: ✅ ①sit: 'volunteer to sit'에서 to부정사 뒤 동사원형으로 정상. ✅ ②listen: to sit, listen, and provide의 병렬 구조로 정상. ✅ ③were chosen: 할머니들이 '선정되었다'는 수동태로 정상. ❌ ④listened: 원문은 listening skills. 명사 skills를 수식하는 현재분사(동명사). '경청 기술'. listened(과거분사)는 의미가 맞지 않음.
det.tip: listening skills(경청 기술): listening은 동명사로 명사 skills를 수식. writing skills, reading skills과 같은 패턴.

questions.passage: When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients. The members of these groups have ①<u>experiencing</u> similar struggles. They can easily relate to and ②<u>support</u> one another. This is because most of ③<u>them</u> come from the same community. The program has been incredibly ④<u>successful</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 비슷한 어려움을 겪은 경험이 있기 때문이다.
det.analysis: ❌ ①experiencing: 원문은 'have experienced'. 현재완료(have + p.p.) 구문. experiencing(현재분사)은 완료형에 쓸 수 없음. ✅ ②support: '지지하다'로 정상. ✅ ③them: 'most of them'에서 대명사로 정상. ✅ ④successful: 형용사로 정상.
det.tip: 현재완료 = have/has + p.p.(과거분사). have experiencing(×) → have experienced(○). 완료형에는 반드시 과거분사.

questions.passage: I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community ①<u>struggle</u> with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. One patient of mine was going through a ②<u>effortless</u> time after her mom passed away. I knew that I could help heal their ③<u>wounded</u> hearts by supporting them. I've seen how it can make a ④<u>difference</u> in people's lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 엄마가 돌아가신 후 힘든 시간을 보내고 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①struggle: 정신 건강 문제로 '고심하다' → 적절. ❌ ②effortless: '쉬운, 힘들지 않은'. 원문은 difficult(힘든). 엄마를 잃은 후 '힘든' 시간인데 effortless(수월한)는 정반대. ✅ ③wounded: '상처받은' 마음 → 적절. ✅ ④difference: 'make a difference(변화를 만들다)' → 적절.
det.tip: difficult(힘든) ≠ effortless(쉬운). effort(노력) + -less(없는) = 노력이 필요 없는.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people ①<u>dealing</u> with issues such as depression or anxiety. Grandmothers were chosen because they are also very ②<u>vulnerable</u>, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. They have the ability to ③<u>engage</u> in meaningful discussions. The sessions are provided by respected ④<u>elderly</u> women from the community.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 매우 믿음직한(reliable) 분들인데, 이것이 정신 건강 지원 노력에 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①dealing: '문제를 다루는' → 적절. ❌ ②vulnerable: '취약한'. 원문은 reliable(믿을 수 있는). 정신 건강 지원에 중요한 자질로 '취약한'은 부적절. ✅ ③engage: '참여하다' → 적절. ✅ ④elderly: '노인의' → 적절.
det.tip: reliable(믿을 수 있는) vs vulnerable(취약한): 상담가에게 필요한 자질은 신뢰성(reliability)이다.

questions.passage: Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. When the Friendship Bench program started in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people. I needed to find a way to bring psychiatry into the community. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services.
questions.stem:
다음 내용이 본문과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"우정 벤치 프로그램이 2006년에 시작되었을 때, 짐바브웨에는 1,200만 명 이상의 인구를 위해 일하는 정신과 의사가 11명뿐이었다."

det.korean: 2006년에 짐바브웨 정신과 의사가 11명뿐이었다.
det.analysis: 원문 'there were only eleven psychiatrists serving Zimbabwe's population of over twelve million people'와 정확히 일치. T가 정답.
det.tip: 수치 문제에서는 숫자를 정확히 대조: eleven(11명), 2006(년도), twelve million(1,200만).

questions.passage: At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.
questions.stem:
다음 내용이 본문과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"우정 벤치 프로그램은 처음에 40명의 자원봉사자 할머니들과 함께 시작했다."

det.korean: 처음에 14명의 자원봉사자 할머니들과 시작했다.
det.analysis: 원문은 'only fourteen(14명)'인데 제시문은 '40명'으로 수치가 다름. F가 정답.
det.tip: fourteen(14) ≠ forty(40). 숫자를 혼동하기 쉬운 함정. 영어 수사를 정확히 읽는 것이 중요.

questions.passage: In 2022, we provided face-to-face counseling to about 90,000 patients in Zimbabwe. Now, Friendship Benches are available in more than twenty different regions around the country. We've also started expanding the program, and we now offer online counseling through an app.
questions.stem:
다음 내용이 본문과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"우정 벤치 프로그램은 현재 앱을 통한 온라인 상담도 제공하고 있다."

det.korean: 앱을 통해 온라인 상담을 제공한다.
det.analysis: 원문 'we now offer online counseling through an app'과 정확히 일치. T가 정답.
det.tip: expanding the program의 구체적 예시가 online counseling through an app이다.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 할머니들은 환자들에게 정서적 지원을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① emotional support
❌ ② financial assistance
❌ ③ medical prescriptions
❌ ④ legal advice
할머니들은 벤치에 앉아 이야기를 듣고 정서적 지원을 제공하는 대화 치료 프로그램. ② financial assistance(재정적 도움), ③ medical prescriptions(처방전), ④ legal advice(법률 자문)는 대화 치료의 성격과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: emotional support(정서적 지원): 전문 의료 행위가 아닌 공감과 대화를 통한 심리적 지원.

questions.passage: That sounds like a great way to continue the support and build a sense of community. When the sessions with the grandmothers are over, patients are encouraged to join a community support group made up of former patients of the program. The members of these groups can easily relate to and support one another. This is because most of them come from the same community and have experienced __________. The program has been incredibly successful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그들 대부분이 같은 지역 사회 출신이고 비슷한 어려움을 겪은 경험이 있기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① different cultures
❌ ② professional training
❌ ③ academic challenges
✅ ④ similar struggles
같은 커뮤니티 출신이라 서로 공감하고 지지할 수 있다는 맥락에서 'similar struggles(비슷한 어려움)'가 적절. ① different cultures, ② professional training, ③ academic challenges는 정신 건강 문제 맥락과 불일치.
det.tip: relate to(공감하다): 비슷한 경험을 했기에 서로의 어려움을 이해하고 공감할 수 있다는 논리.

questions.passage: The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This shocked me, as I had never considered such a problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and receive medical treatment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Dr. Chibanda의 환자는 병원에서 치료를 성공적으로 받았다.
짐바브웨 사람들은 교통비 부담 없이 병원에 갈 수 있다.
Dr. Chibanda는 환자가 교통비 때문에 치료를 못 받는 것에 충격받았다.
Dr. Chibanda는 이전부터 교통비 문제를 인지하고 있었다.

det.korean: 환자가 버스비를 감당하지 못해 도움을 받을 수 없었고, 이것이 충격을 주었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① Dr. Chibanda의 환자는 병원에서 치료를 성공적으로 받았다.
❌ ② 짐바브웨 사람들은 교통비 부담 없이 병원에 갈 수 있다.
✅ ③ Dr. Chibanda는 환자가 교통비 때문에 치료를 못 받는 것에 충격받았다.
❌ ④ Dr. Chibanda는 이전부터 교통비 문제를 인지하고 있었다.
③ 원문 'she was unable to afford the bus ride' + 'This shocked me'와 일치. ① 환자는 치료를 받지 못했음. ② 교통비가 어렵다고 명시. ④ 'had never considered such a problem'이므로 이전에는 몰랐음.
det.tip: 일치/불일치 문제에서는 각 선택지의 핵심 정보를 원문과 하나씩 대조해야 함.

questions.passage: Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. I knew that I could help heal their wounded hearts by supporting them.
questions.stem: Grandma Moyo에 대한 다음 설명 중 옳지 않은 것은?
ch: 지역 사회의 정신 건강 문제에 관심을 갖고 참여했다.
환자들의 상처받은 마음을 치유하는 것을 돕고 있다.

det.korean: 약 8년간 자원봉사를 해왔다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 본명은 Judith Moyo이다.
✅ ② 지역 사회의 정신 건강 문제에 관심을 갖고 참여했다.
❌ ③ 환자들의 상처받은 마음을 치유하는 것을 돕고 있다.
❌ ④ 약 18년간 자원봉사를 해왔다.
② 원문은 'about eight years(약 8년)'인데 선택지는 '약 18년'으로 수치 불일치. ① 'my name is Judith Moyo' 일치. ③ 'many people struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it' 일치. ④ 'help heal their wounded hearts' 일치.
det.tip: eight(8) vs eighteen(18): 비슷한 발음의 숫자를 혼동하게 만드는 전형적인 함정.

questions.passage: ① Grandmothers were chosen for the program because they are deeply connected to the community. ② Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. ③ At the beginning, we started with only forty volunteer grandmothers. ④ But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문과 다른 부분이 포함된 문장은?

det.korean: 처음에 겨우 14명의 자원봉사자 할머니들과 시작했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
✅ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
③에서 'forty(40명)'는 원문의 'fourteen(14명)'과 다름. ①②④는 원문과 동일.
det.tip: fourteen(14) ≠ forty(40). 원문의 수치를 정확히 기억해야 오류를 찾을 수 있다.

questions.passage: The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support. Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program? Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 세션을 제공하는 여성들이 갖춘 자질 중 하나를 본문 전체에서 찾아 **영어** 1단어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: 상담가의 자질: 경청 기술, 공감, 의미 있는 토론 참여 능력.
det.analysis: 원문 'qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions'에서 1단어 자질은 empathy.
det.tip: empathy(공감): 다른 사람의 감정을 이해하고 함께 느끼는 능력. 상담에서 핵심 자질.

det.korean: 그녀는 심지어 자신의 사업을 시작했다.
det.analysis: 원문 'she has even started her own business!'에서 회복 후 한 일은 'started her own business'. 지문에서 해당 구절을 의도적으로 빼서 전체 원문 기억을 테스트.
det.tip: back on track: 다시 정상 궤도에 오른. 회복 후 자신의 사업까지 시작한 성공 사례.

questions.passage: On today's show, we are going to learn about special park benches in Zimbabwe called Friendship Benches. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 지역 사회 기반의 정신 건강 지원 프로그램

det.korean: 이 글의 주제는 지역 사회 기반의 정신 건강 지원 프로그램이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 짐바브웨의 공원 벤치 디자인
❌ ② 노인 여성들의 은퇴 후 활동
❌ ③ 우울증 치료를 위한 약물 개발
✅ ④ 지역 사회 기반의 정신 건강 지원 프로그램
우정 벤치 프로그램은 지역 사회의 할머니들이 공원 벤치에서 대화 치료를 제공하는 정신 건강 서비스. ① 벤치 디자인이 아니라 프로그램, ② 은퇴 후 활동이 핵심이 아님, ③ 약물이 아닌 대화 치료.
det.tip: 주제 파악: 세부 사항이 아닌 글 전체를 관통하는 핵심 메시지를 찾아야 한다.

questions.passage: The idea came from an experience I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients had become severely depressed. However, she couldn't get help because she was unable to afford the bus ride to the hospital. Furthermore, there has been a lack of psychiatrists in the country for many years. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

"The Friendship Bench program was created to overcome the   (A)   of mental health care by using community   (B)   to provide support."

det.korean: 정신 건강 관리의 장벽을 극복하기 위해 지역 사회 자원봉사자를 활용.
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) barriers — (B) volunteers
❌ ② (A) benefits — (B) professionals
❌ ③ (A) barriers — (B) professionals
❌ ④ (A) benefits — (B) volunteers
(A) barriers: 교통비, 정신과 의사 부족 등이 '장벽'. benefits(이점)는 문제가 아니라 결과. (B) volunteers: 할머니들은 전문가가 아닌 '자원봉사자'. professionals(전문가)는 할머니들의 역할과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: 요약 문제: 원인(barriers) → 해결책(volunteers)의 논리 흐름을 파악해야 한다.

det.korean: 정신 건강 문제에 대한 도움을 구하는 것은 부끄러워할 일이 아닙니다.
det.analysis: 핵심 구조: Seeking(동명사 주어) + is nothing to be ashamed of(보어). 'nothing to be ashamed of'는 '부끄러워할 것이 없다'는 관용 표현.
det.tip: 동명사 주어: Seeking help ~은 '도움을 구하는 것'으로 문장의 주어. nothing to V: ~할 것이 없다.

questions.ans: Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of.
